dedupe_keys.name: hydropower expansion and reservoir management for increased glacier melt in iceland landsvirkjun

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study shows how Landsvirkjun, the national power company of Iceland, adapts hydropower to glacier melt. Hydropower supplies 73 percent of Icelandic electricity and the largest stations are fed by glacial rivers; almost all glaciers have lost mass since the early 1990s, runoff is expected to peak within 50 years and fall towards zero by 2200, and 2015 inflow scenarios were about 10 percent above predictions from historical records. With Nordic research partners, Landsvirkjun corrects inflow series using observed temperature and precipitation and glacier area-volume-elevation curves adjusted to climate model trends, feeds them into a hydrological model, and updates reservoir management every five years with yearly calibration; new designs consider flows 15 years ahead and beyond. Research cost about 1 million euros and design changes tens of millions; capacity has risen about 10 percent, including an extension at Burfell built in just over two years from 2016, and larger reservoirs add flood buffer. The page, published in 2018 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML. Coverage is Iceland. Caveats: projections are uncertain, so alternate plans such as curtailment agreements are kept. It illustrates climate-adjusted inflow modelling for hydropower capacity planning.
